settings.choosePokemon: Pick a Pokémon you caught on the Switch
settings.allowIllegalHelp: Off: RockAssistent won't send the Switch a Pokémon PKHeX considers illegal. On: each trade with an illegal one still asks for confirmation.

checks.udev_rule_optional: Optional: udev rule so the port is always named {{path}}.
checks.switch_test_ok: Switch test passed: the room was found on channel {{channel}} and decrypted. Radio and prod.keys confirmed.

checks.card_test_failed: The {{model}} card ({{phy}}) failed the test. See the result below.

checks.network_manager_unconfigured: NetworkManager may interfere with trading. Set it up below (recommended).

checks.switch_test_needs_keys: Upload a valid prod.keys (Keys item) before the Switch test.

checks.worker_appimage_missing: The network component has not been installed from the AppImage yet. Use the button below.
checks.worker_appimage_outdated: The installed network component is from another RockAssistent version. Use the button below to update it.

checks.esp32_firmware_ok: The RockAssistent firmware answered on the port ({{target}}): communication OK.
checks.esp32_firmware_other_chip: This board's firmware is for another chip ({{target}}), but you picked {{model}}. Check which ESP32 you have.

cardTest.title: Card test ({{phy}})
cardTest.help: The test puts the card in monitor mode and transmits the frames the Switch's room uses. It takes about 10 seconds and needs neither the Switch nor prod.keys.
cardTest.password: The first time, the system asks for the administrator password (the system asks, not RockAssistent). It then stays valid until you close the app.
cardTest.offline: During the test, this card's normal Wi-Fi is turned off. It comes back by itself at the end.
cardTest.offlineInternet: Heads up: this card is the PC's internet. During the test (and during trades) the internet drops and comes back by itself at the end.
cardTest.needsWorker: First sort out the network component (see the list below).
cardTest.needsTools: First install the missing programs (see the list below).
cardTest.waitPassword: If the system password window shows up, type the administrator password.
cardTest.apOk: The card opened a network in AP mode: it trades with every game.
cardTest.apNo: The card couldn't open a network in AP mode: it trades only with FireRed/LeafGreen.

codes.passed: The card passed: monitor mode and transmission work.
codes.passed_no_rx: The card transmitted but received no frames.
codes.passed_some_channels: The card passed but didn't tune to every channel.
codes.monitor_failed: The card refused monitor mode. Its driver doesn't work for LDN.
codes.channel_failed: The card entered monitor mode but couldn't tune to any channel. Another program may be using it.
codes.tx_failed: The card couldn't transmit in monitor mode. Its driver doesn't work for LDN.
codes.card_test_crashed: The test stopped with an error. Try again; if it keeps happening, export the report from the summary.

cardTest.optionsMany: You can test again, pick another card in the list above, or use an ESP32 instead of the Wi-Fi card.
cardTest.optionsOne: You can test again or use an ESP32 instead of the Wi-Fi card.

network.title: NetworkManager
network.help: For each trade, the engine creates a temporary wireless connection (named starting with "ldn"). If NetworkManager tries to manage it, the trade authenticates but never completes. This setting tells it to ignore those connections; your internet is unchanged.
network.confirmText: RockAssistent will create these two files (as administrator) and reload the NetworkManager configuration, without dropping your current connection:

switchTest.title: Switch test
switchTest.before: Before you start, on the Switch:
switchTest.stepOpen: open FireRed or LeafGreen and go to the Direct Corner (2nd floor of the Pokémon Center);
switchTest.stepLeader: choose to be the Leader and stay on the room's waiting screen;
switchTest.stepNear: keep the Switch close to the PC (within about 2 meters).
switchTest.noJoin: RockAssistent only listens: it does not join the room, and the Switch gets no join request.
switchTest.offline: During the test (up to {{seconds}} seconds), this card's normal Wi-Fi is turned off. It comes back on its own at the end.
switchTest.needsCard: First pass the card test (Network component item).
switchTest.waitPassword: If the system password window appears, type the administrator password.
switchTest.undecryptable: {{count}} advertisement(s) that did not decrypt, on channel(s) {{channels}}
switchTest.unusable: Channels the card could not tune: {{channels}}
switchTest.sweeps: {{sweeps}} pass(es) over the channels in {{seconds}} s

codes.found_decrypted: Room found and decrypted! Radio and prod.keys confirmed.
codes.found_not_decrypted: The room was found but could not be decrypted: the prod.keys is not right.
codes.other_session: The prod.keys works (a session from another game was decrypted), but the FireRed/LeafGreen room did not show up.
codes.monitor_failed: The card did not enter monitor mode. Run the card test again (Network component item).
codes.channel_failed: The card could not tune any channel. Another program may be using the card.
codes.scan_failed: The search stopped with an error. Try again; if it keeps happening, export the report in the summary.
codes.engine_error: The network component could not start the search. Try again; if it keeps happening, export the report in the summary.

found_not_decrypted: Use the prod.keys dumped from your own Switch, with the system up to date. Keys from another console or an old version do not work.
Upload the file again in the Keys item and repeat the test.
other_session: Check that you opened the Direct Corner as the Leader and are still on the waiting screen.
If another Switch nearby is playing in local mode, move it away or turn its local mode off.
not_found: Check that the Switch is in the Direct Corner as the Leader, on the waiting screen (the room disappears when you leave it).
Move the Switch closer to the PC.
Check that the Switch is not in airplane mode.
If it keeps happening, run the card test again (Network component item): reception may be the problem.

hints.missing_master_key_12: Your prod.keys does not have the key for the newer LDN protocol (master_key_12). Updated consoles use that protocol: dump the keys again with the system up to date.

switchTest.esp32Band: The ESP32 only sees rooms on 2.4 GHz (channels 1, 6 and 11, the ones the Switch uses). If the Switch is connected to a 5 GHz network, the room may not show up: disconnect the Switch from the internet and open the room again.
switchTest.needsFirmware: First check the ESP32 firmware in the ESP32: firmware and USB port item.

esp32fw.title: ESP32 firmware
esp32fw.help: The ESP32 needs the pokeldn firmware to talk to the Switch (every game uses the same one). RockAssistent ships the right firmware for each chip and flashes it by itself, over USB.
esp32fw.identifyHelp: Identifying and checking restart the board for a moment; it goes back to normal by itself.
esp32fw.flashConfirmText: Everything on the ESP32 will be replaced. It takes 30 seconds to 2 minutes. Don't unplug the board until it's done.
esp32fw.bootTitle: If the board doesn't enter flashing mode
bootSteps: Hold the BOOT button (sometimes labeled IO0 or B).
While holding it, press and release RESET (EN or RST).
Release BOOT and click "Flash the firmware" again.
After flashing, press RESET once so the board goes back to normal.

workerInstall.title: Install the network component
workerInstall.why: The network component is the part of RockAssistent that uses the Wi-Fi card as administrator. It ships inside the AppImage, but the system only lets it run as administrator after it is copied to a system folder.
workerInstall.password: The system asks for the administrator password to copy it (the system asks, not RockAssistent).
workerInstall.remove: You can remove it at any time in Settings.

state.missing: Not installed. It is needed to trade with the Wi-Fi card.
state.outdated: Installed, but from another RockAssistent version. Update it to use the Wi-Fi card.

workerInstall.removeHelp: Deletes /usr/local/lib/traderock and the polkit policy. The system asks for the administrator password. Your Pokémon and settings are not deleted.

about.title: About RockAssistent
about.releases: Packages and source code of every version:
about.creditsHelp: RockAssistent uses these projects. The licenses were checked in each one's source code.

login.title: Sign in to RockAssistent
login.intro: This RockAssistent is open on the home network. Sign in with your account to see your vault and trade.
login.noAccount: No account? Ask whoever runs RockAssistent on the PC to create one for you.

errors.too_many_attempts: Too many wrong attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.
errors.csrf: This page is out of date. Reload it and try again.

server.title: Server mode (phones and other PCs)
server.onHint: Other people on the home network can sign in. See Settings.
server.intro: While the app is open, other people on the same network (your home Wi-Fi or cable) open RockAssistent in their phone or PC browser, sign in with an account and use their own vault. Since there is only one radio, trades wait in a queue, one at a time.
server.warningInternet: Never open this port on your router or put RockAssistent on the internet. Anyone outside could try to get in.
server.warningHttp: The connection is not encrypted (http): someone on the same network could see passwords. Use it only on trusted networks, with passwords you don't use anywhere else.
server.interfaceHelp: How this PC connects to the home network. RockAssistent listens only there.
server.portHelp: A number from 1024 to 65535. The default is 8337.
server.radioWifi: The Wi-Fi card that does the trades leaves the network during a trade, so it can't be used here.
server.noInterface: No connected network interface was found. Connect the PC to the home network.
server.noInterfaceWifi: This PC's only network is the Wi-Fi card that does the trades. Plug in a network cable or a second Wi-Fi adapter (or use the ESP32 as the radio).
server.offOnStart: Server mode always starts off when the app opens.
server.openOnPhone: On the phone (same network), point the camera at the code or type the address:
server.qrAlt: QR code with RockAssistent's network address

errors.interface_not_found: That interface is no longer connected. Pick another one.
errors.interface_is_radio: That is the Wi-Fi card that does the trades. Pick another interface.
errors.bind_failed: Couldn't use that port (another program may be using it). Try another port.

server.localOnly: This screen only opens in the RockAssistent window on the PC itself.
server.windowsFirewall: On Windows, the installer already allowed RockAssistent through the Firewall, on "Private" networks only. If the phone can't open it, check in Windows Settings → Network & internet that the home network is set to "Private network".

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.intro: Each account has its own vault, history and "My trainer", and starts with the demo Pokémon. The connection setup, prod.keys and the radio stay in this PC window only.
accounts.rolesHelp: Administrators can also create and manage accounts and remove people from the queue. Users only use their own vault and trade.
accounts.usernameHelp: 3 to 24 unaccented letters, numbers, dot, hyphen or _.
accounts.deleteBody: This person's vault (Pokémon, boxes, tags and history) will be deleted too. This can't be undone.

errors.username_taken: There is already an account with that name.
errors.username_invalid: Invalid name: use 3 to 24 unaccented letters, numbers, dot, hyphen or _.
errors.password_invalid: The password must have 8 to 128 characters.
errors.owner_fixed: The PC owner's account can't be deleted, disabled or made a user.

queue.title: In the queue
queue.position: You are number {{position}} in the queue
queue.starting: It's your turn: the trade is starting…
queue.help: There is only one radio, so trades happen one at a time. When your turn comes, the trade starts by itself: keep the Switch ready, in the Direct Corner room as Leader, and keep this page open.
queue.freeNow: The radio is free: the trade starts as soon as you click.
queue.ahead_one: There is {{count}} trade ahead of you. You join the queue and yours starts by itself when it's your turn.
queue.ahead_other: There are {{count}} trades ahead of you. You join the queue and yours starts by itself when it's your turn.
queue.removed: An administrator removed you from the queue. You can join again whenever you want.

status.ownerPc: The connection is on the owner's PC
status.activate: Real trades still need to be turned on

login.homeOnly: Only works on your home network

home.intro: Send Pokémon from your PC to FireRed / LeafGreen and keep the ones you receive.
home.tradeSub: Pick up to 6 Pokémon and send them to the Switch.
home.vaultSub: View, organize and edit your Pokémon.
home.createSub: Build a legal Pokémon in a few clicks.
home.readySub: Open the Direct Corner on the Switch and start.
home.demoSub: Meanwhile, you can use everything in demo mode.
home.activateTitle: All tested: just turn real trades on

title.radio: Radio to talk to the Switch

what.system: With the Wi-Fi card, RockAssistent controls the card directly, which only works with Linux installed on the PC (not a virtual machine or WSL). With an ESP32, any system works.
what.keys: Switches talk in encrypted form. The prod.keys file has the keys to understand that conversation. It is unique to your console and comes from it.
what.radio: It is what talks “over the air” with the Switch: your PC's Wi-Fi card or a small ESP32 board on USB. One of the two is enough.
what.driver: A small program that lets the Wi-Fi card speak the Switch's “language”. Installed once; it asks for the administrator password when used.
what.usb: The ESP32 needs the right firmware and the PC needs permission to talk to it over the USB port.
what.game: In FireRed/LeafGreen, wireless trading happens at the Direct Corner (2nd floor of the Pokémon Center). You create the room as Leader and RockAssistent joins as if it were another Switch.
what.switch: A quick test that trades nothing: RockAssistent looks for your Switch's room and checks that it can understand the conversation.

desc.systemWindows: Windows: trades use an ESP32 over USB
desc.systemWarn: The Wi-Fi card does not work here. Use an ESP32.
desc.system_wsl: You are on WSL: the Wi-Fi card does not work here. Use an ESP32 or real Linux.
desc.system_vm: Virtual machine: the Wi-Fi card does not work here. Use an ESP32.
desc.system_windows: Windows: trades use an ESP32 over USB
desc.keysSkipped: Skipped: trades stay in demo mode
desc.keysMissing: File extracted from your own Switch
desc.radioNone: Choose the Wi-Fi card or an ESP32
desc.radioWifi: Wi-Fi card: choose which card to use
desc.radioEsp32: ESP32 over USB: choose the board and port
desc.driverEspOk: Firmware answering on the chosen port
desc.game: Direct Corner unlocked (about 20–40 min of play)
desc.switchOk: Room found and decrypted. Radio and prod.keys confirmed.
desc.switchIdle: Optional: open the room as Leader on the Switch and click Test. Takes up to {{seconds}} s.

radio.wifiSub: Uses your PC's card. Needs real Linux.
radio.esp32Sub: Cheap little board. Works on any PC and keeps your internet up.

conn.esp32Guide: How to choose and connect the ESP32
conn.summarySub: Each item shows what is missing and how to fix it.
conn.reportHint: Report without keys, names or personal paths
conn.activateHelp: Everything tested. Just turn the radio on for trades.
conn.keysNote: Only use the keys from your own console. Do not download them or share them. RockAssistent keeps the file just for you and never sends it over the network.
conn.remote: The connection is set up on the owner's PC. Here you only follow the status.
keysSteps: On your unlocked Switch, run Lockpick_RCM.
Copy the prod.keys file from the SD card to the PC.

lan.title: Home network (Sword/Shield only)
lan.sub: Sword/Shield can also trade over your home network, with no ESP32, Wi-Fi card or prod.keys. The Switch and this computer must be on the same network.
lan.step1: In the game, open Options and press L + R + the left stick together: a message says LAN mode is on.
lan.step2: The link code is not used: any Switch in LAN mode on the same network finds RockAssistent.

settings.trainerSub: Your save's data. Created Pokémon arrive as yours and always obey.
settings.trainerTip: Name and ID appear on the in-game trainer card. The secret ID does not: send one of your Pokémon in a trade and use “Take from a received Pokémon”.
settings.themeSub: Light, dark or same as the system.
settings.illegalSub: Each trade with an illegal one still asks for confirmation.
settings.illegalTip: “Illegal” means PKHeX thinks this Pokémon could not exist in the original game (impossible stats, moves or origin). The game may refuse the trade. Leave it off if unsure.
settings.defaultsOk: The default values work for almost everyone.
settings.tempoTip: Only change these if trades fail. Attempts: how many times it looks for the room. Approve the join: how long you have to say Yes on the Switch. Idle in the room and maximum time: after that the trade is cancelled.
settings.engineTip: The engine is what talks to the Switch. The simulation fakes a Switch so you can learn the steps. The Wi-Fi card and the ESP32 show up after they are set up in Connection.
settings.serverTip: Turns this PC into a small home server. Anyone on the same Wi-Fi opens the address in their phone's browser and uses their own vault. Trades use this PC's radio, one at a time.
settings.accountsTip: Each person has their own vault, history and trainer. A user only trades and organizes their own vault. An administrator also creates accounts and can remove people from the queue.
settings.devTip: Starting over clears the connection choices (radio, card, port and tests) so you can set it up again. prod.keys stays stored. In development, you can also simulate another kind of PC without changing anything for real.
settings.devSub: Simulate another kind of PC (development only) or start the setup over.
settings.restartSub: Start the connection setup from scratch.

trade.title: Trade with the Switch
trade.demoBanner: Everything works, but trades are simulated until the connection is ready.
trade.teamTip: RockAssistent pretends to be another Switch with this team. Mark who goes to your game. The team needs 2 or more Pokémon because the game does not let you trade the last one. All of them are stored in the vault before starting.
trade.whichGame: Which game are you trading with?
trade.nameTip: It is the name you will approve in the request to join the room. Up to 7 characters, no accents (the game has no “ã” or “ç”). You can use . - ! ?
trade.prepSub: Do this in the game before clicking Start.

prep.title: Direct Corner
prep.sub: Talk to the attendant on the left and choose trade.

prep.title: Be the Leader
prep.sub: Create the room. The Switch waits.

prep.title: Near the PC
prep.sub: Keep the Switch close to the PC or the ESP32.

trade.prepMore: The Direct Corner unlocks after about 20 to 40 minutes of play. The Switch creates a local wireless network and RockAssistent joins it as if it were a second Switch. The connection sometimes needs a few attempts: RockAssistent retries on its own.
trade.queueNote: You are on the network: the trade goes into the PC's queue.
trade.whichGameSub: Pick the game and the version on the Switch.

games.soon: With a real Switch, coming soon (already works in demo mode)

trade.linkCodeTip: Eight digits. On the Switch, use the same code for the trade. Leave it blank to trade without a code.
trade.linkCodeLgpeTip: In Let's Go, the code is three Pokémon picked in order. Pick here the same ones you will pick on the Switch. Left blank, the default is three Pikachu.
trade.offersTip: Each Pokémon you pick goes to the Switch, one per trade, in this order. This game needs no filler Pokémon.
trade.otherGame: It is from {{game}}: you can move it to another game in the vault
trade.tradeBackTip: For a Switch Pokémon that evolves by trade: after each trade, RockAssistent sends the Pokémon it received straight back (it evolves on the Switch) and gets back the one it sent. In the end, the vault is unchanged.

live.savedInbox: The received Pokémon was stored in the Inbox.
live.anyCode: of your choice (LAN mode ignores the code)

vault.search: Search by name, number, nickname or trainer
vault.ivEvTip: IVs are the Pokémon's “genes” (0 to 31), already set. EVs are training (up to 255 per stat and 510 in total). Both raise the stats.
vault.natureTip: In the 3rd generation the nature comes from an internal number (PID). Changing the nature generates the Pokémon again, like in Create.
vault.natureRegenerates: With another nature, RockAssistent generates the Pokémon again (like in Create) so it stays possible in the game. IVs may change.
vault.savedIllegal: Saved, but PKHeX reports legality problems

errors.pokemon_duplicate: The result is the same as another Pokémon in the vault.

builder.movesHint: Leave empty to use the moves it would know at this level.
builder.moreOptions: More options (item, IVs, EVs, origin, trainer)
builder.ivTip: IVs are the Pokémon's “genes” (0 to 31). EVs are training (up to 255 per stat and 510 in total). With “any”, RockAssistent picks possible values.
builder.advancedBanner: Raw data, like in PKHeX. Nothing is fixed automatically: the panel on the side shows what is wrong.
builder.legalTip: Checked by PKHeX {{version}}. “Notes” do not make the Pokémon illegal.

about.intro: Trades Pokémon with FireRed and LeafGreen on the Switch using the game's local wireless. Your PC (or an ESP32) pretends to be a second Switch in the Direct Corner room.
about.keysSub: Never downloads, shows or sends prod.keys.
about.offlineSub: It only checks GitHub for new versions, and you can turn that off.
about.freeSub: AGPL-3.0: use, study and modify it.

ui.building: This area is still under construction. It will show up here soon.

activities.engineUnsupported: The chosen connection doesn't do other activities. Use the ESP32, the Wi-Fi card or demo mode in Settings → Connection.
activities.whichGameSub: Mystery Gift on FireRed/LeafGreen and Sword/Shield; raids on Sword/Shield and Scarlet/Violet; Union Circle on Scarlet/Violet.

gift.title: Which gift?
gift.sub: Pick a ready-made gift, an official event or open a gift file.
gift.fileHelp: Open a gift file ({{types}}). RockAssistent doesn't download gifts: use files you already have.

progress.swshConfirm: The console only hears the gift and doesn't say when it gets it. Once the card shows up in the game and you accept it, click Done.
progress.raidBattle: The battle is on the console. When it ends, click Done.

result.frlg: Gift delivered. Save the game and talk to the delivery man on 2F of any Pokémon Center.
result.swsh: Done. If the card reached the game, the gift is there.

errors.busy: The radio is busy with a trade or another activity. Wait for it to finish.
errors.gift_unknown: This gift doesn't exist for the chosen game.
errors.gift_file_wrong_type: This file type doesn't work for the chosen game.
errors.gift_file_invalid: The file isn't a valid gift.
errors.gift_file_other_game: This gift is for another game.
errors.gift_not_received: The console didn't receive the gift. Check that it was on the Mystery Gift search screen and try again.
errors.activity_engine_unsupported: The chosen connection doesn't do other activities.
errors.activity_game_unsupported: This game has no other activities in RockAssistent yet.
errors.raid_invalid: This raid isn't for this game, or a field is missing.
errors.raid_event_invalid: This event doesn't have that boss, version or stage.
errors.raid_not_started: The battle didn't start. Check the console steps and try again.
errors.unknown_pokemon: That Pokémon is no longer in the vault.
errors.pokemon_wrong_game: That Pokémon is from another game.
errors.circle_invalid: Check the task, the Pokémon and the level.
errors.circle_not_done: The task didn't finish. Check the console steps and try again.
errors.circle_not_started: The circle didn't start. Check the console steps and try again.

raid.title: Which raid?
raid.sub: You choose who opens the room: RockAssistent or your console.

about.max-raid-host: RockAssistent opens a Max Raid with the boss you choose and fights with your Pokémon. The console joins through Y-Comm.
about.max-raid-join: The console opens the raid at a den (Invite Others) and RockAssistent joins to fight at your side.
about.lair-host: RockAssistent opens a Dynamax Adventure with the chosen legendary. Once the adventure starts, it leaves and a game partner takes over.
about.lair-join: The console opens the Dynamax Adventure at the Max Lair (Invite Others) and RockAssistent joins to help.
about.tera-raid-host: RockAssistent opens a Tera Raid with the boss you choose. The console searches through the Poké Portal with code 4970.
about.tera-raid-join: The console opens the Tera Raid at a crystal (Challenge as a group) and RockAssistent joins with your Pokémon.

raid.noPokemon: You have no Pokémon for this game in the vault. Make one in the builder or import a file.
raid.choosePokemon: Choose a Pokémon from the vault
raid.offerHelp: It fights at your side in the raid.
raid.gigantamax: Gigantamax (only if the species has it)
raid.codeHelp: 8 digits. Use the same on the console; leave blank for none.
raid.svBossHelp: The vault Pokémon becomes the raid boss.
raid.svEventHelp: Optional: an already distributed event Tera Raid.
raid.playersHelp: How many consoles will join. Empty seats go to game partners.
raid.seedHelp: 8 hexadecimal digits. The same seed gives the same raid.
raid.moveAutoHelp: Before starting, RockAssistent picks the move that works best against the boss (type, power and same-type bonus). It uses that move for the whole battle.
raid.targetHelp: The Pokémon your console opened. Without it, RockAssistent uses its strongest move.

circle.title: Union Circle
circle.sub: The console opens the circle and RockAssistent joins.

about.quests: RockAssistent clears Blueberry Quests for your console: every Snacksworth legendary, or the BP you choose. Then it leaves the circle.
about.encounters: RockAssistent makes the wild Pokémon you choose appear around your player, to battle and catch.

circle.codeHelp: The 4 digits you used on the console.

progress.running: The circle is running on the console. To finish, close the circle on the console or click Done.

logs.title: Logs
logs.sub: What RockAssistent, pokeldn and the ESP32 flasher recorded in the last {{days}} days. Newest first.
logs.copyFailed: Could not copy. Use Save file.
logs.privacy: Logs stay on this PC and never carry the prod.keys: keys, long numbers and Pokémon data are removed before writing. Only send the file to whoever is helping you.

update.title: Updates
update.neverChecked: Never checked for a new version.
update.auto: Check for a new version when the app opens (at most once a day)
update.privacy: The check only reads RockAssistent's releases page on GitHub. Nothing from your PC is sent, and the prod.keys never leaves it.
update.manual: This copy does not update itself. Download the new version from the Release page:

confirm.windows_installer: RockAssistent downloads the installer, checks the file and runs the setup. Windows asks for administrator permission, as in the first install. The app closes and opens again on its own at the end.
confirm.app_image: RockAssistent downloads the new AppImage, checks the file, replaces the current one and opens again.
confirm.deb: RockAssistent downloads the package, checks the file and installs it. The system asks for your administrator password. The app closes and opens again on its own at the end.

stages.restarting: Done. RockAssistent will close and open again.

errors.update_check_failed: Could not reach GitHub. Check the internet and try again.
errors.update_download_failed: The download stopped. Check the internet and try again.
errors.update_hash_mismatch: The downloaded file does not match the one published in the Release. Nothing was installed.
errors.update_asset_missing: The Release has no file for this install. Download it from the Release page.
errors.update_cancelled: Administrator permission was not given. Nothing was installed.
errors.update_no_permission: No permission to replace the AppImage file. Move the AppImage to a folder of yours or download from the Release page.
errors.update_manual: This copy does not update itself. Download from the Release page.
errors.busy: Finish the trade or activity in progress before updating.
errors.update_failed: The update failed. See the Logs tab in Settings.

dex.title: Pokédex
dex.sub: Every Pokémon, with the data of the game you pick.
dex.error: Couldn't load the Pokédex. Try again in a moment.
dex.notFound: This Pokémon is not in the Pokédex.
dex.notInGame: This Pokémon doesn't exist in {{game}}. General data still shows; moves, locations and texts stay empty.

general.noFlavor: No Pokédex entry in this game.
general.damageHelp: How much each move type deals to this Pokémon: ×2 and ×4 are weaknesses, ×½ and ×¼ resistances and ×0 immunity.

encounters.empty: Not found in the wild in this game. Check the General tab: maybe you can get it by evolution, egg or trade.

moves.empty: No moves in this list in this game.

saves.soon: Coming soon: the saves in your folders that have this Pokémon show up here.
saves.found_one: Shows up {{count}} time in your saves.
saves.found_other: Shows up {{count}} times in your saves.
saves.none: None of your saves has this Pokémon.

move.notFound: This move is not in the Pokédex.
move.notInGame: This move doesn't exist in {{game}} or nobody learns it there.
move.effectInEnglish: The effect text is in English for now.
move.learners: Who learns it in this game
move.noLearners: Nobody learns this move in this game.

ability.notFound: This ability is not in the Pokédex.
ability.effectInEnglish: The effect text is in English for now.

item.notFound: This item is not in the Pokédex.
item.effectInEnglish: The effect text is in English for now.

typeChart.title: Type chart
typeChart.sub: How much damage each move type deals to each Pokémon type.
typeChart.help: Row = move type; column = type of the Pokémon taking the hit. ×2 is super effective, ×½ not very effective and ×0 has no effect. Empty means normal damage (×1).

guides.title: Guides
guides.sub: Quick facts about the games, the mechanics, VGC and the legends, no fluff.

sectionsSub.games: Walkthrough, bosses, TMs, exclusives and legendaries for each game.

guides.notFoundHint: The address may be wrong or the guide may have moved.

block.unknownHint: Check the directive name in the guide.

boxes.title: Boxes
boxes.localOnly: Saves live in folders on the PC, so they only show up in the RockAssistent window on the computer. On the phone, use the app vault.
boxes.newHere: Create a Pokémon in this slot
boxes.newInInbox: Saved to the vault, but the chosen slot was already taken: it went to the Inbox.
boxes.noFolders: Choose the folders where your emulator keeps its saves. RockAssistent looks for the files there and shows their boxes here.
boxes.noSaves: No saves found in the folders. Check the folders in Settings or tap "Look again".
boxes.dragHint: Drag between the save and the vault. Dropping on another Pokémon of the same save swaps them.
boxes.dropInbox: Drop a Pokémon from the save here to keep it in the Inbox.
boxes.moveToSave: Move or copy to a save
boxes.modeHelp: Copy leaves the original where it is. Move takes it out of the source (in a save, with a backup first; in the vault, it goes to the trash). Attach copies and keeps both linked: the vault updates when the Pokémon changes in the save.

modeHint.copy: The original stays where it is.
modeHint.move: It leaves the source. The save gets a backup before it changes.
modeHint.attach: Copies and keeps it linked to the save: changes in the save reach the vault.

boxes.noWritableSaves: No save that can be changed. Add a save folder in Settings.
boxes.convertHint: If the save is from another game, the Pokémon is converted like Pokémon HOME does (when possible).
boxes.converted: The Pokémon was converted to the destination game, like Pokémon HOME does.
boxes.doneWithBackup_one: Done! The old save was kept as a backup.
boxes.doneWithBackup_other: Done! The old saves were kept as backups ({{count}}).
boxes.noFamily: This game doesn't trade with RockAssistent, so the Pokémon can't go to the vault or to a trade. You can copy it to another save of the same kind.

errors.save_unwritable: Couldn't write the save (folder without permission or file in use). Nothing was changed.
errors.save_read_only: This save is view only: RockAssistent can't write this format.
errors.save_wrong_game: This Pokémon can't go to this save's game
errors.save_game_unsupported: Pokémon from this game don't go to the vault (the game doesn't trade with RockAssistent).
errors.save_changed: The save changed on disk (did the emulator save?). We reloaded the boxes: check and try again.
errors.save_not_found: The save wasn't found. Tap "Look again".
errors.slot_occupied: That slot is already taken. Pick an empty one.
errors.slot_locked: That slot is locked in the game (battle team or locked box).
errors.slot_invalid: That slot doesn't exist in this save.
errors.slot_repeated: The same slot showed up twice.
errors.attach_wrong_game: You can only attach when the save is from the Pokémon's own game. Use Copy.
errors.attach_invalid: Attach only works between the vault and a save.
errors.sav_wrong_game: This Pokémon is in another format and doesn't fit this save.
errors.sav_too_big: File too big to be a save
errors.sav_unreadable: No permission to read the file
errors.folder_invalid: Use the folder's full path (for example, /home/you/saves or C:\Saves).
errors.verify_failed: The write failed the check; the save was restored from the backup.
errors.pokemon_not_found: This Pokémon isn't in the vault anymore.
errors.invalid_pokemon: This Pokémon's data couldn't be read.
errors.no_window: Open RockAssistent in the PC window to choose the folder.
errors.box_not_found: That vault box doesn't exist anymore. Pick another.
errors.box_full: That vault box is full. Pick another one or the Inbox.
errors.evolve_not_available: This Pokémon does not evolve by trade.
errors.evolve_wrong_target: That evolution does not apply to this Pokémon. Open the list again.

foldersCard.title: Save folders
foldersCard.sub: Where your emulator keeps its saves. The Boxes screen shows the boxes of these files.

where.mgba: mGBA (GBA): in the same folder as the ROM, a .sav file.
where.melonds: melonDS (DS): in the same folder as the ROM, a .sav file (or .dsv in DeSmuME).
where.switchEmu: Ryujinx / yuzu (Switch): in the emulator's save folder ("Open save folder" menu); the file is called main.
where.citra: Citra (3DS): in Citra's sdmc folder, under Nintendo 3DS/…/title/…/data; the file is called main.

foldersCard.whereNote: You can pick a parent folder: RockAssistent also looks in subfolders.

boxes.cloneVaultHint: The vault keeps one copy of each Pokémon. To have copies, use "Move or copy to a save".
boxes.cloneNoSpace: There is no free slot in this save for the copy.

evolveDialog.title: Trade-evolve {{name}}
evolveDialog.help: The app does the evolution a trade would trigger, without another game. Trainer, moves and everything else stay the same.
evolveDialog.none: This Pokémon does not evolve by trade (or it is holding an Everstone).
evolveDialog.needsItem: In a trade it must hold {{item}}. The app evolves it even without the item.
evolveDialog.usesItem: It is holding {{item}}: the item is used up by the evolution.
evolveDialog.tradeWith: In the game, it must be traded for a {{species}}.
evolveDialog.illegal: PKHeX found problems after the evolution. It is still saved, but a trade may refuse it:
evolveDialog.vaultDone: It evolved into {{species}}. The previous one is in the trash.

trades.title: Trades
trades.sub: Trade Pokémon with the Switch or join raids and the Union Circle through the same radio.

trade.title: Trade
trade.sub: Send and receive Pokémon with your console.

raid.title: Raids
raid.sub: Max Raid and Dynamax Adventure (Sword/Shield) and Tera Raid (Scarlet/Violet).

gifts.title: Mystery Gift
gifts.sub: Send event gifts to FireRed/LeafGreen and Sword/Shield through the same radio as trading.

nuzlocke.title: Nuzlocke
nuzlocke.sub: Track your runs: the next boss, the area you are in, your team and who fell along the way.
nuzlocke.emptyActive: No run in progress. Start one with "New run".

rules.title: Rules
rules.customHelp: Write any other rules you want to follow (just a reminder; the app doesn't check them).
rules.customPlaceholder: E.g.: no items in battle, limited Pokémon Center

firstEncounterOnly.name: First encounter
firstEncounterOnly.help: Only the first Pokémon in each area counts.

nicknameRequired.name: Nickname required
nicknameRequired.help: Every Pokémon you catch gets a nickname.

faintIsDeath.name: Fainted means dead
faintIsDeath.help: A Pokémon that faints goes to the graveyard.

speciesClause.name: Species clause
speciesClause.help: A species you already caught doesn't count: you can try again in the area.

shinyClause.name: Shiny clause
shinyClause.help: A shiny can always be caught, even in a used area.

dupesClause.name: Dupes clause
dupesClause.help: Covers the whole evolution line: a Pidgeotto counts as a Pidgey.

levelCapRequired.name: Level cap required
levelCapRequired.help: No one on the team goes above the next boss's level.

newRun.title: New run
newRun.name: Name
newRun.versionHelp: Bosses and encounters change from one version to the other.

run.confirmDeleteText: The run, the team and the graveyard are gone for good.
run.confirmChampionText: Congratulations! The run is kept with the finished ones and won't change anymore.
run.confirmWipeText: The whole team fell. The run is kept with the finished ones and won't change anymore.
run.pausedNote: Paused run. You can still record everything; resume whenever you want.

boss.title: Next boss
boss.allDefeated: Every boss defeated. Now just finish the run!

area.title: Current area
area.noAreas: We don't have the areas of this game yet.
area.noEncounters: No known encounters in this area. Use "Record another" to write down what showed up.

statusHelp.party: Caught and sent to the team.
statusHelp.box: Caught and sent to the box.
statusHelp.failed: Fled or fainted: the area is used.
statusHelp.missed: Encounter that doesn't count (e.g. a dupe under a clause): the area stays free.

area.noEncounterConfirm: Mark the area with no encounter?
area.noEncounterConfirmText: The area becomes used: under the first encounter rule, you won't be able to record another catch here.

team.title: Team
team.empty: No one on the team yet. Record a catch in the current area.

death.title: {{name}} died
death.causePlaceholder: E.g.: a crit from Brock's Onix

editDialog.title: Edit {{name}}
editDialog.movesHelp: Pick up to 4 among the moves it already learned by level.

trainers.title: Trainers in the area
trainers.unavailable: Regular trainers aren't available for this game. The bosses show up in the next boss card.

graveyard.empty: No one has died yet. Keep it that way!

errors.unknown_version: This version isn't from this game.
errors.unknown_boss: This boss isn't from this version.

hunt.title: Hunt Counter
hunt.sub: Count encounters until the shiny shows up. You can keep several hunts going at once.
hunt.emptyActive: No hunt in progress. Start one with "New hunt".

wizard.title: New hunt
wizard.noGames: We found no game with a way to hunt this Pokémon in our data.
wizard.counterStep: {{name}}: follows the counter on its own.

counter.cumulativeHelp: With this many encounters, you already had a {{percent}} chance of finding it.
counter.giveUpText: The hunt leaves "In progress" and stays in the finished list as given up.
counter.notesPlaceholder: Route, time of day, anything you want to remember...
counter.hotkeysHint: Shortcuts: {{inc}} adds and {{dec}} removes. Change them in Settings → Preferences.
counter.hotkeysHintGlobal: Global shortcut on: {{inc}} adds and {{dec}} removes even with the app behind another window.
counter.deleteText: The counter, time and notes are gone for good.

errors.method_not_in_game: This method doesn't exist in this game.
errors.modifier_not_in_game: This modifier doesn't apply to this game.
errors.invalid_delta: You can only add or remove up to 100 at once.

hotkeys.title: Hunt Counter shortcuts
hotkeys.sub: They work with the counter page open and the window in front. Not inside text fields.

global.label: Global shortcut (works with the app in the background)
global.help: For emulator players: the keys count even with another window in front. While RockAssistent is open, other programs stop receiving them, and so do the app's own text fields.
global.textKeyWarning: This key types or deletes text: with the global shortcut on, it disappears from every program (you can't type a space or delete, not even here). Prefer F1–F12 or a combo with Ctrl or Alt.

reasons.wayland: Wayland doesn't allow global shortcuts; use the window shortcut.
reasons.no_x11: Couldn't talk to X11 (no X display); use the window shortcut.
reasons.in_use: Another program already uses one of these keys. Pick another and turn it on again.
reasons.unsupported_os: This system has no global shortcuts; use the window shortcut.
reasons.remote: The global shortcut can only be turned on in the PC window.

errors.hotkeys_same: The two shortcuts can't be the same.
errors.hotkey_invalid: That key can't be a shortcut.
errors.hotkey_unsupported: That key can't be a global shortcut. Use letters, digits, F1–F12, arrows or the numeric keypad.
errors.hotkey_in_use: Another program already uses that key. Pick another.
errors.hotkey_global_unsupported: The global shortcut doesn't work on this system.
errors.local_only: The global shortcut can only be turned on in the PC window.

errors.analyze: Couldn't analyze right now. Try again.
errors.import: Couldn't import right now. Try again.

report.title: Analysis: {{name}}
report.skipped: Left out of the analysis (not in Scarlet/Violet or past 6):
report.defenseHint: How much damage each attacking type does to each member. Red: takes more; green: takes less or none.

report.coverageHint: Types of the team's attacking moves (status moves don't count).
report.limits: Uses types and moves as in Scarlet/Violet. Doesn't count abilities (Levitate, Water Absorb...), items, Mega Evolution or Stat Points.
